hook_text: It looks like an old wire lying in the dust. It can kill a child in a second.
clip_script: Some cables in South African communities are called izinyoka, snakes, because they snake through the sand and along fences. They are illegal connections: electricity taken from an overhead line or a neighbour without permission. A proper house circuit has three guards: a circuit breaker, an earth leakage unit and an earth wire. An illegal cable has none. So when a child picks it up, the current flows through the child and nothing switches it off. Thin cables also overheat and start fires that spread from shack to shack. And when too many illegal connections load a transformer, it burns out, and the whole area goes dark, including every family that pays. Treat every loose cable as live. Stay away. Report it to Eskom or your municipality.
visual_style: Slow pan along a cable in the sand; a diagram of the three missing guards fading out; a transformer glowing red; a neighbourhood's lights switching off.
pacing: Quiet open, steady explanation, a sharp beat on the transformer, a firm safety message to close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and share the safety rules with a younger child at home.
